QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc(Bazett) 380 ms. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Of note, the same-day clinic note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing despite the patient's atrial fibrillation history.

568cb149 (man, b.1978), 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at 104/min with a discrete P wave (upright in II/aVF, inverted in aVR) about 140 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, no BBB; axis +42 degrees. The T wave peaks ~190 ms and returns towards baseline by ~290 ms, the later deflection at ~430 ms being the next P wave: QT 346 ms, QTc(Bazett) 455 ms. Prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a low-amplitude T wave, QT ~275 ms and QTc ~434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is well under 60 ms.

5f3dcdb5 (man, b.1979), 2024-05-21. Regular rhythm at 108/min with a P wave ~125 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +39 degrees (normal). T wave peaks ~230 ms and ends ~310 ms after the R: QT 348 ms, QTc(Bazett) 470 ms - borderline prolonged, partly reflecting Bazett over-correction at this rate. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

5f74c4bf (woman, b.1948), 2026-06-10 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm, RR 0.35-0.65 s (CV 0.16) with no reproducible atrial deflection in the PR window (beat-to-beat PR-window correlation 0.74 with a P amplitude below noise): atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 136/min, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis +2 degrees, QT 290 ms, QTc(Bazett) 450 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 h 23 min earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at 132/min with QTc 441 ms, so there is no change between the two. Both contradict the same-day note describing sinus rhythm at 72/min (raised as a documentation-conflict item).

71a27b6b (woman, b.1942), 2025-08-02. Regular sinus rhythm at 69/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block. QT 402 ms, QTc(Bazett) 430 ms. The frontal plane shows a tall R in I/aVL with a deep S in II, III and aVF and a nearly isoelectric lead II; the QRS area vector computes to about -29 degrees, i.e. at the upper limit of normal (borderline leftward) rather than frank left axis deviation. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) was sinus at 61/min, QTc 401 ms, with a markedly different, apparently reversed limb-lead pattern (computed axis about -172 degrees); rhythm and QTc are unchanged (difference 29 ms), so no tracked change.

735c5ea5 (man, b.1968), 2024-05-23. Regular rhythm at 98/min with a P wave ~115 ms before each QRS: sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +5 degrees (normal); QT 308 ms, QTc(Bazett) 392 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

752d15e2 (woman, b.1968), 2025-12-25. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min, PR 150 ms, QRS 74 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +25 degrees (normal), QT 376 ms, QTc(Bazett) 412 ms - all within normal limits. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. This remains the patient's most recent tracing, which matters because escitalopram was started on 2026-08-01 without a follow-up ECG (raised separately).

76202c51 (woman, b.1961), 2024-11-15. Irregularly irregular rhythm with RR alternating between about 0.70 and 1.17 s (relative MAD 0.03 but 62% of successive RR differences exceed 60 ms) and no organised P wave - the averaged PR window shows only 0.03 mV of activity and the beat-to-beat correlation is 0.47. This is atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 61/min, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +32 degrees, QT 426 ms, QTc(Bazett) 401 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave and PR 176 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; QTc is essentially unchanged (399 to 401 ms).

7ec7078a (woman, b.1975), 2025-03-09. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +66 degrees (normal), QT 420 ms, QTc(Bazett) 414 ms. Prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) is virtually identical (sinus 62/min, PR 116 ms, QTc 439 ms), so there is no rhythm change and the QTc difference is only 25 ms. This is the most recent tracing available, predating the haloperidol started on 2026-09-15.

807d2a03 (woman, b.1965), 2025-08-23. Regular sinus rhythm at 83/min (RR CV 0.005), PR 146 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +57 degrees (normal), QT 342 ms, QTc(Bazett) 403 ms. Entirely normal tracing. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

8e77dd0b (woman, b.1972), 2020-06-19. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min, PR 154 ms, QRS 62 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 406 ms, QTc(Bazett) 459 ms. Prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm (75/min, PR ~152 ms) but with a later T-wave offset, QT 464 ms and QTc 517 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 58 ms, just short of the 60 ms threshold, so no change is recorded, though the trend is toward normalisation.

1cf9e585 (man, b.1963), 2021-01-18. Very regular RR 0.494-0.502 s (rate 121/min) with a discrete P wave 180 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. PR ~185 ms, QRS 92 ms (no BBB), frontal axis +53 degrees, QT 284 ms, QTc 402 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QTc 399 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc differs by only 3 ms, so no significant change.

23069939 (man, b.1970), 2023-10-08. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +49 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad and late (peak ~360 ms, end ~455 ms after the R): QT 484 ms, QTc(Bazett) 516 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) was sinus at 75/min with QT 320 ms and QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 159 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The interval prolongation is relevant to the current escitalopram order and is flagged separately as a QT safety item.

28dcf33b (woman, b.1971), 2024-04-19. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 121/min (RR 0.496 s, CV 0.005) with an upright P wave preceding each QRS at a PR of ~135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 72 ms, no BBB; axis +71 degrees (normal). T wave peaks ~180 ms and ends ~280 ms after the R (the later deflection at ~370 ms is the next P wave): QT 308 ms, QTc(Bazett) 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2edf1f64 (man, b.1993), 2021-08-23 10:07. Regular sinus rhythm at 102/min, PR ~148 ms, QRS 82 ms, axis +62 degrees (normal), QT 324 ms, QTc 421 ms. No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 40 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, QTc 416 ms), so there is no interval or rhythm change.

3886cafb (man, b.1946), 2024-10-24. Regular rhythm at 52/min with a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms): sinus bradycardia. QRS 82 ms, no BBB; axis +40 degrees (normal); QT 428 ms, QTc(Bazett) 397 ms. Despite a long-standing atrial fibrillation diagnosis this tracing is in sinus rhythm. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus bradycardia (58/min, one ectopic beat) with QTc 390 ms, so no rhythm change and no significant QTc change.

4365e125 (man, b.1981), 2024-12-05 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular tracing, RR 0.492-0.496 s (122/min) with a small P wave ~130 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 298 ms, QTc 424 ms. The frontal QRS forces are small and directed inferiorly/rightward (net negative lead I, positive III) giving an axis of about +130 degrees - right axis deviation. Prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) was also sinus at 100/min with QTc ~429 ms, so no rhythm or QTc change; overall voltages are low on both tracings.

4c48ec6f (man, b.1947), 2025-11-24. Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min, PR 178 ms (normal), QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +68 degrees. The T wave is broad, peaking ~390 ms and ending ~470 ms after the R: QT 512 ms, QTc(Bazett) 520 ms - prolonged. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, before amiodarone was started) was sinus bradycardia at 49/min with QT 462 ms and QTc 410 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 110 ms, more than the 60 ms threshold. This is consistent with amiodarone effect and is raised separately as a QT safety item.

51d2190c (man, b.1966), 2024-09-17 - the day after atrial fibrillation was coded. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, CV 0.28, relative MAD 0.16) with no reproducible P wave before the QRS: beat-to-beat correlation of the PR window is only 0.25, i.e. the atrial activity is disorganised. This is atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101/min, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 72 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis -56 degrees (left axis deviation), QT 322 ms, QTc(Bazett) 414 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: 94abdf17 (man, b.1976), 2025-06-23. Regular rhythm at 55/min with a well-formed P wave before every QRS: sinus bradycardia. The P wave begins about 255 ms and peaks 210 ms before QRS onset, giving a PR interval of roughly 215 ms - above 200 ms, so first-degree AV block is present. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +4 degrees (normal); QT 388 ms, QTc(Bazett) 369 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51/min with PR 190 ms and QTc 352 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is only 17 ms.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; the drug first appears in the medication list of that day's note). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order cbe91d0f). Because the start predates 2026-03-01 the earlier 2025-09-01 memo governs and the window is 30 days (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day rule), so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc 441 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order 88943096). The start is on/after 2026-03-01 so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 2026-09-24. (For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a, valid to 2026-12-29; the drug first appears in that day's note, the brief inpatient course of 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01 having ended seven months earlier). The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264, valid to 2027-01-04; the drug first appears in that day's note). The start is on/after 2026-03-01 so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Paul Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation/d6b3bad5), four days after the change, so the requirement was met. The nurse telephone note of 2026-09-23 is only a tamsulosin refill at an unchanged dose and is not a further dose change.

The anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (DocumentReference/9579a764) records 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol'. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1945-10-26 (age 80). Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 (DocumentReference/5116e8ae) through 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference/a41e9ebb). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: CHF 1 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110 / heart failure I509), hypertension 1 (I10), age >=75 2, diabetes 1 (E119/E11649), prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction V1254 with hemiplegia and dysphagia following cerebral infarction I69351/I69391), vascular disease 1 (coronary atherosclerosis I2510, old MI), female 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1955-09-07 (age 71). Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission (Condition/66dd1300), the same admission that documented an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. No CHF, diabetes or vascular disease coded. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Man born 1960-10-11 with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulants from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was re-issued the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26). Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug (clinic memo of 2025-01-15) and is current: order 8de890c6 of 2026-04-23 is valid to 2027-01-02. This patient's most recent ECG is 108018814 (2023-10-08), sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 484 ms and QTc (Bazett) 516 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review. The 2024-05-14 clinic note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the tracing. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A current ECG and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order 1014aca9 of 2026-07-29 is valid to 2027-01-05 (amiodarone has been continuous since it was started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit). The most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 512 ms and QTc (Bazett) 520 ms, above the 500 ms threshold; the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07, before amiodarone) had a QTc of 410 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 110 ms on treatment. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) are normal - potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL. Prescriber review of amiodarone dose/continuation and a repeat ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order 7f787d30 of 2026-05-29 is valid to 2026-12-25. The most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 490 ms and QTc (Bazett) 530 ms, above the 500 ms threshold; the previous ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17) had a QTc of 436 ms. Note that 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended for QT reasons in patients over 60 or on interacting drugs. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a current ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 (man, b.1973). Regular rhythm at 81/min with gradual respiratory variation (RR 0.66-0.86 s), a consistent upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS and a fixed PR of ~185 ms: sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc(Bazett) 380 ms. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Of note, the same-day clinic note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing despite the patient's atrial fibrillation history.

568cb149 (man, b.1978), 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at 104/min with a discrete P wave (upright in II/aVF, inverted in aVR) about 140 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, no BBB; axis +42 degrees. The T wave peaks ~190 ms and returns towards baseline by ~290 ms, the later deflection at ~430 ms being the next P wave: QT 346 ms, QTc(Bazett) 455 ms. Prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a low-amplitude T wave, QT ~275 ms and QTc ~434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is well under 60 ms.

5f3dcdb5 (man, b.1979), 2024-05-21. Regular rhythm at 108/min with a P wave ~125 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +39 degrees (normal). 5f74c4bf (woman, b.1948), 2026-06-10 19:36. 735c5ea5 (man, b.1968), 2024-05-23. Regular rhythm at 98/min with a P wave ~115 ms before each QRS: sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +5 degrees (normal); QT 308 ms, QTc(Bazett) 392 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

752d15e2 (woman, b.1968), 2025-12-25. 76202c51 (woman, b.1961), 2024-11-15. 7ec7078a (woman, b.1975), 2025-03-09. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +66 degrees (normal), QT 420 ms, QTc(Bazett) 414 ms. Prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) is virtually identical (sinus 62/min, PR 116 ms, QTc 439 ms), so there is no rhythm change and the QTc difference is only 25 ms. This is the most recent tracing available, predating the haloperidol started on 2026-09-15.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; the drug first appears in the medication list of that day's note). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc 441 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order 88943096). The start is on/after 2026-03-01 so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 2026-09-24. (For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a, valid to 2026-12-29; the drug first appears in that day's note, the brief inpatient course of 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01 having ended seven months earlier). The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained, could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264, valid to 2027-01-04; the drug first appears in that day's note). The start is on/after 2026-03-01 so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Paul Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation/d6b3bad5), four days after the change, so the requirement was met. The nurse telephone note of 2026-09-23 is only a tamsulosin refill at an unchanged dose and is not a further dose change.

The anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (DocumentReference/9579a764) records 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol'. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1945-10-26 (age 80). Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 (DocumentReference/5116e8ae) through 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference/a41e9ebb). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: CHF 1 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110 / heart failure I509), hypertension 1 (I10), age >=75 2, diabetes 1 (E119/E11649), prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction V1254 with hemiplegia and dysphagia following cerebral infarction I69351/I69391), vascular disease 1 (coronary atherosclerosis I2510, old MI), female 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1955-09-07 (age 71). Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission (Condition/66dd1300), the same admission that documented an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. No CHF, diabetes or vascular disease coded. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Man born 1960-10-11 with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulants from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was re-issued the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26). Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

7ec7078a (woman, b.1975), 2025-03-09. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +66 degrees (normal), QT 420 ms, QTc(Bazett) 414 ms. 807d2a03 (woman, b.1965), 2025-08-23. Regular sinus rhythm at 83/min (RR CV 0.005), PR 146 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +57 degrees (normal), QT 342 ms, QTc(Bazett) 403 ms. Entirely normal tracing. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

8e77dd0b (woman, b.1972), 2020-06-19. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min, PR 154 ms, QRS 62 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 406 ms, QTc(Bazett) 459 ms. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +63 degrees (normal); QT 380 ms, QTc(Bazett) 422 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

The T wave is broad and late (peak ~360 ms, end ~455 ms after the R): QT 484 ms, QTc(Bazett) 516 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) was sinus at 75/min with QT 320 ms and QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 159 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The interval prolongation is relevant to the current escitalopram order and is flagged separately as a QT safety item.

QRS 72 ms, no BBB; axis +71 degrees (normal). T wave peaks ~180 ms and ends ~280 ms after the R (the later deflection at ~370 ms is the next P wave): QT 308 ms, QTc(Bazett) 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2edf1f64 (man, b.1993), 2021-08-23 10:07. Regular sinus rhythm at 102/min, PR ~148 ms, QRS 82 ms, axis +62 degrees (normal), QT 324 ms, QTc 421 ms. No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 40 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, QTc 416 ms), so there is no interval or rhythm change.

3886cafb (man, b.1946), 2024-10-24. Regular rhythm at 52/min with a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms): sinus bradycardia. QRS 82 ms, no BBB; axis +40 degrees (normal); QT 428 ms, QTc(Bazett) 397 ms. Despite a long-standing atrial fibrillation diagnosis this tracing is in sinus rhythm. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus bradycardia (58/min, one ectopic beat) with QTc 390 ms, so no rhythm change and no significant QTc change.

4365e125 (man, b.1981), 2024-12-05 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular tracing, RR 0.492-0.496 s (122/min) with a small P wave ~130 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 298 ms, QTc 424 ms. The frontal QRS forces are small and directed inferiorly/rightward (net negative lead I, positive III) giving an axis of about +130 degrees - right axis deviation. Prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) was also sinus at 100/min with QTc ~429 ms, so no rhythm or QTc change; overall voltages are low on both tracings.

4c48ec6f (man, b.1947), 2025-11-24. Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min, PR 178 ms (normal), QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +68 degrees. The T wave is broad, peaking ~390 ms and ending ~470 ms after the R: QT 512 ms, QTc(Bazett) 520 ms - prolonged. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, before amiodarone was started) was sinus bradycardia at 49/min with QT 462 ms and QTc 410 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 110 ms, more than the 60 ms threshold. This is consistent with amiodarone effect and is raised separately as a QT safety item.

51d2190c (man, b.1966), 2024-09-17 - the day after atrial fibrillation was coded. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, CV 0.28, relative MAD 0.16) with no reproducible P wave before the QRS: beat-to-beat correlation of the PR window is only 0.25, i.e. the atrial activity is disorganised. This is atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101/min, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 72 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis -56 degrees (left axis deviation), QT 322 ms, QTc(Bazett) 414 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: bbad4581 (man, b.1984), 2026-04-29. Regular sinus rhythm at 70/min, PR 148 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, QT 352 ms, QTc(Bazett) 379 ms. The frontal plane is unusual: lead I and II are deeply negative while aVR is positive, and the QRS area vector computes to about -170 degrees, which falls in the extreme axis (-90 to -180) range. The precordial R-wave progression is normal with transition at V3-V4, a pattern that in practice often indicates left/right arm lead reversal, so the limb-lead placement should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. This tracing was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started, outside the required 14-day window (raised separately).

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 (man, b.1973). QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc(Bazett) 380 ms. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Of note, the same-day clinic note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing despite the patient's atrial fibrillation history.

568cb149 (man, b.1978), 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at 104/min with a discrete P wave (upright in II/aVF, inverted in aVR) about 140 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, no BBB; axis +42 degrees. The T wave peaks ~190 ms and returns towards baseline by ~290 ms, the later deflection at ~430 ms being the next P wave: QT 346 ms, QTc(Bazett) 455 ms. Prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a low-amplitude T wave, QT ~275 ms and QTc ~434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is well under 60 ms.

5f3dcdb5 (man, b.1979), 2024-05-21. Regular rhythm at 108/min with a P wave ~125 ms before each QRS: sinus tachycardia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +39 degrees (normal). T wave peaks ~230 ms and ends ~310 ms after the R: QT 348 ms, QTc(Bazett) 470 ms - borderline prolonged, partly reflecting Bazett over-correction at this rate. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

5f74c4bf (woman, b.1948), 2026-06-10 19:36. 71a27b6b (woman, b.1942), 2025-08-02. Regular sinus rhythm at 69/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block. QT 402 ms, QTc(Bazett) 430 ms. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

Because the start predates 2026-03-01 the earlier 2025-09-01 memo governs and the window is 30 days (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day rule), so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. (For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

No ECG has been recorded since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 (DocumentReference/5116e8ae) through 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference/a41e9ebb). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1955-09-07 (age 71). Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission (Condition/66dd1300), the same admission that documented an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. No CHF, diabetes or vascular disease coded. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Man born 1960-10-11 with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulants from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was re-issued the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26). Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A current ECG and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; the drug first appears in the medication list of that day's note). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

Because the start predates 2026-03-01 the earlier 2025-09-01 memo governs and the window is 30 days (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day rule), so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc 441 ms.

The only ECG on file, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 2026-09-24. (For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; the drug first appears in the medication list of that day's note). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

Because the start predates 2026-03-01 the earlier 2025-09-01 memo governs and the window is 30 days (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day rule), so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc 441 ms.

(For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). That outside tracing, if obtained, could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report arrives.

No ECG has been recorded since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 (DocumentReference/5116e8ae) through 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference/a41e9ebb). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Man born 1960-10-11 with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulants from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was re-issued the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26). Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

A current ECG and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; amiodarone first appears in the medication list in that visit's note). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was satisfied. (That ECG's QTc of 520 ms is itself prolonged and is raised separately as a QT_SAFETY item.)

Because the start predates 2026-03-01 the earlier 2025-09-01 memo governs and the window is 30 days (the 2026-03-01 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day rule), so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc 441 ms.

(For information, that late ECG showed sinus rhythm at 70/min, QTc 379 ms.) Escitalopram remains active (order 0d9b142c, valid to 2027-01-03).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a, valid to 2026-12-29; the drug first appears in that day's note, the brief inpatient course of 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01 having ended seven months earlier). The start is on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). That outside tracing, if obtained, could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264, valid to 2027-01-04; the drug first appears in that day's note). The start is on/after 2026-03-01 so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the anticoagulation protocol (standing order of 2024-06-01), so this is a qualifying dose change and the 2026-03-01 memo required a follow-up INR within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. No post-change INR has been obtained, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1955-09-07 (age 71). Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission (Condition/66dd1300), the same admission that documented an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. No CHF, diabetes or vascular disease coded. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Man born 1960-10-11 with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulants from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was re-issued the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26). Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug (clinic memo of 2025-01-15) and is current: order 8de890c6 of 2026-04-23 is valid to 2027-01-02. This patient's most recent ECG is 108018814 (2023-10-08), sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 484 ms and QTc (Bazett) 516 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review. The 2024-05-14 clinic note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the tracing. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A current ECG and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

QRS 88 ms, no BBB; axis +42 degrees. The T wave peaks ~190 ms and returns towards baseline by ~290 ms, the later deflection at ~430 ms being the next P wave: QT 346 ms, QTc(Bazett) 455 ms. T wave peaks ~230 ms and ends ~310 ms after the R: QT 348 ms, QTc(Bazett) 470 ms - borderline prolonged, partly reflecting Bazett over-correction at this rate. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm, RR 0.35-0.65 s (CV 0.16) with no reproducible atrial deflection in the PR window (beat-to-beat PR-window correlation 0.74 with a P amplitude below noise): atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 136/min, so no measurable PR interval. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, i.e. before the change; the home INR of 3.4 is not a chart result and in any case preceded the change. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but current medications are only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg; the DOACs given during the January 2025 admission (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) were all stopped or completed and no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24.

Woman born 1955-09-07 (age 71). Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission (Condition/66dd1300), the same admission that documented an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension 1 (I10), age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2 (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia and hemiparesis of the left non-dominant side I69354), female 1. No CHF, diabetes or vascular disease coded. Anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, yet the current regimen in the 2026-07-10 clinic note is only carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference/96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Man born 1952-09-16 with atrial flutter (Condition/a7f25b6c) on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference/8fcbd349) document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RR CV 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded on that admission (Condition/54ec94da) and warfarin was started the same day, so the note's rhythm statement is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and should be corrected.

Despite this a new outpatient apixaban 5 mg twice daily order was written on 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28, so the drug is current. A major, recent, clinically overt GI bleed with an explicit instruction to hold pending cardiology review means anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the bleeding source, timing of resumption and choice of agent/dose.

Both are therefore current on 2026-09-24, and the note's own medication list shows apixaban AND rivaroxaban together. Two full-dose oral anticoagulants at once carries a high bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

items.explanation: Man born 1955-08-23 (age 71). Atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission (Condition/7010d0e5) and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference/174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at a score of >=2 in men, but the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - no warfarin or DOAC order is active as of 2026-09-24. Note the coded hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22), so bleeding risk should be weighed when starting therapy.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current: order c6f532e9 of 2026-08-22 is valid to 2027-01-05 (continuous since 2024-12-13). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with first-degree AV block (PR ~205 ms), QT 548 ms and QTc (Bazett) 537 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is also on warfarin (interacting drug) and had a dose reduction on 2026-09-10. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required; the only ECG on file predates more than four years of amiodarone therapy.

Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 380 ms, well below the 500 ms review threshold.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a, valid to 2027-01-02; the drug first appears in that day's note). Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference/b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08.
